posts.note: Publication announcement for the American Journal of Therapeutics psychedelic primer series; no forward-looking claims.
44-word note with a graphic about the announced Optum acquisition of Stewart (Steward) Health.
Argument essay for Medicaid coverage of TMS; mostly present-tense cost-effectiveness evidence. The coverage call is normative; two borderline items logged for recall.
Esketamine drug review. Quoted cost-effectiveness model projections are third-party data and were not logged.
Evidence review of ketogenic diet for bipolar disorder; hypothetical trial-design musings not logged.
Cover-song and minimalism essay; no forecasts.
Podcast blurb plus the RAMHT NYC 2024 event announcement (May 5th, 2024).
Essay against physician-assisted suicide for psychiatric illness (Dutch ter Beek case). Prognosis claims are general clinical statements, logged as borderline.
Follow-up on media coverage of the Dutch euthanasia case. The recommendation is normative; one causal claim with a predictive reading logged.
Podcast episode blurb; one trivial musing about naming produced audio.
RAMHT NYC 2024 event announcement (May 5th, 2024, during APA 2024); speaker attendance plans are CONTROL candidates. Colin Kealey (Neurosigma) is also implied as a speaker but not logged separately.
Second ransomware extortion of Change Healthcare (RansomHub). Three substantive calls plus a content promise. RansomHub's own 12-day threat is third-party and not logged directly.
99-word screenshot post. 'Stay tuned.' is an implicit content promise, too short and trivial to log.
Satirical Change Healthcare post. 'You'll be working at UnitedHealthcare in no time' is a pure joke with no sincere reading and was not logged.
Seroquel review. Five 'a priori' bets logged with forward_looking false: they concern existing evidence the author will check in later articles, not a future world state.

statements.quote: the announcement of the Optum Acquisition of Stewart Health brings 50% of physicians in MA under the employ of Optum
statements.context: One-line note with a graphic. The author says the announced Optum acquisition of Stewart (Steward) Health puts 50% of Massachusetts physicians under Optum's employ. At the post date (2024-03-27) the deal is announced, not closed.
statements.note: Borderline: states the effect of an announced, pending acquisition as a present fact; the 50% figure is the author's characterization.

statements.quote: More tomorrow…
statements.context: Closing line promising more content the next day on the Optum/Steward Health topic.
statements.note: Own-newsletter content promise; low forecast value; coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: We have data that demonstrate psychiatric interventions t hat work rapidly might provide the most robust savings for the economics of Medicaid.
statements.context: Argument that state Medicaid plans should cover TMS. Because Medicaid enrollment averages about 10 months, the author claims rapid-acting psychiatric interventions such as TMS might give Medicaid the largest savings.
statements.note: Borderline: hedged analytic claim about savings if adopted. The 't hat' typo is verbatim.

statements.quote: The time for Medicaid coverage, given cost-effective remission is happening on the time scale of a week to a month, is now.
statements.context: Conclusion of the argument that Medicaid should cover TMS for treatment-resistant depression, after reviewing cost-effectiveness studies (ICER, QALY data, CTMSS consensus).
statements.note: Normative call for Medicaid TMS coverage; no explicit prediction that coverage will happen.

statements.quote: if you run a Medicaid Plan, I thank you for your coverage policy changes in advance!
statements.context: Closing line of the TMS-for-Medicaid essay. Rhetorical thanks in advance that implies an expectation, or hope, that Medicaid plan administrators will change coverage policy to include TMS.
statements.note: Rhetorical and humorous; reads as a wish more than a forecast. Borderline, logged for recall.

statements.quote: There are many reasons a trial will fail, and the ar ketamine story is unlikely to be over yet.
statements.context: After quoting atai Life Sciences' announcement that PCN-101 (R-ketamine, arketamine, Perception Neuroscience) missed its Phase 2a primary endpoint at 24 hours, the author expects the arketamine development story to continue.
statements.note: Hedged call that the arketamine program is not finished despite the failed Phase 2a.

statements.quote: It’s not yet approved as a monotherapy—treatment on its own.
statements.context: Summary bullet on Spravato (esketamine), approved only with a concurrent oral antidepressant. 'Yet' implies the author expects a possible future monotherapy approval; earlier in the post: 'it is only approved (yet) in adults who have concurrent oral antidepressant treatment.'
statements.note: Implicit forecast carried by 'yet'; borderline. Compound with the earlier '(yet)' aside.

statements.quote: That is likely to require another article.
statements.context: After citing a meta-analysis showing racemic ketamine outperforms esketamine, the author says a full ketamine-versus-esketamine comparison will likely need its own article.
statements.note: Own-newsletter content promise; low forecast value; coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: This science is more likely to be dismissed as flights of fancy by the rest of you
statements.context: The author argues that research on nutritional ketosis for bipolar disorder, often championed by people who themselves have bipolar disorder, is likely to be dismissed by others because of stigma.
statements.note: General tendency claim about how the science will be received; borderline forward-looking.

statements.quote: Until we have well-blinded trials, we should maintain skepticism about how good of an option nutritional ketosis is going to be, and for whom.
statements.context: After reviewing the Stanford pilot (Sethi et al. 2024) and Ede's retrospective chart review, the author says the data are thin and calls for skepticism until blinded trials exist.
statements.note: Mostly normative; the predictive content is an open question about future efficacy. Logged for recall.

statements.quote: This corrosion of close relationships is an accelerating problem for both individual men and society.
statements.context: Podcast intro with Jeremy Fox, LPC, on male friendship. After noting 15% of men report no close friendships, the author claims the loss of male friendships is an accelerating problem.
statements.note: Trend claim ('accelerating'); borderline forward-looking.

statements.quote: It’s a night of thrilling conversations about the future of mental health. It features speakers from…Videra, MDHub, Osmind, Neurosigma, iRxReminder, and…Lykos Theraputics!
statements.context: Announcement of 'Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment NYC 2024' on May 5th, 2024 (Eventbrite link), the second in-person Frontier Psychiatrists event, with the listed speaker companies.
statements.note: Own-event announcement (RAMHT and Videra are the author's organizations); coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: More info to come…but it’s the second IRL The Frontier Psychiatrists event, and we could not be more excited to have you!
statements.context: Same RAMHT NYC 2024 announcement; promise of more information about the May 5th, 2024 event.
statements.note: Content promise about the author's own event; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: They are those who will have a vastly higher likelihood of a personality disorder. Those individuals are also, paradoxically, most likely to go into remission later.
statements.context: Essay against physician-assisted suicide for psychiatric illness, prompted by the Dutch case of Zoraya ter Beek. The author predicts that the cohort most enthusiastic about psychiatric euthanasia will disproportionately have personality disorders, and that these same people are the most likely to remit later.
statements.note: Conditional on offering PAS for psychiatric illness ('If we are going to offer...'); compound claim.

statements.quote: Physician-assisted suicide for psychiatric disorders will inevitably— pointlessly—end the lives of individuals with personality disorders at disproportionate rates.
statements.context: Same essay. Strong call about the outcome of psychiatric euthanasia policy, with the Netherlands as the example.
statements.note: Author calls the policy 'a tragic and catastrophically misinformed decision'.

statements.quote: The porous and suggestible sense of self and poor concept of agency is the problem …a problem that will, in almost everyone, improve with time.
statements.context: BPD prognosis claim. The author cites Gunderson and Zanarini data (85% remission at 10 years, up to 99% at 26 years) and states that BPD improves with time in almost everyone; earlier: 'it's just wait. It will get better.'
statements.note: General clinical prognosis, not a dated forecast; restates 'It will get better.' Borderline.

statements.quote: When we call attention to suicide, when we pay attention to suicidal behavior, we get more death by suicide
statements.context: Follow-up on viral media coverage of the Dutch woman choosing euthanasia. The author argues that attention reinforces suicidal behavior (contagion) and recommends limits on how people promote their euthanasia choice.
statements.note: General causal claim with a predictive reading (more attention leads to more suicide). The recommendation 'Don't give people endless attention for the choice' is normative and not logged. Borderline.

statements.quote: I think these might need a different name in the future—what happens when species diverge in evolution?
statements.context: Intro to the first episode of a produced audio series on Alan Emamdee, D.O. The author says highly produced audio pieces might need a name other than 'podcast' in the future.
statements.note: Trivial own-media musing; low forecast value.

statements.quote: The Next? It’s in NYC….In the middle of the American Psychiatric Association Annual Meeting 2024 time frame. It’s free for APA members, but it is also open to the public.
statements.context: Announcement of the Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment (RAMHT) conference in NYC on May 5th, 2024, after the first one in San Francisco in January 2024.
statements.horizon_text: American Psychiatric Association Annual Meeting 2024 time frame
statements.note: Own-event plan; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: Ben Everett, Ph.D. from Lykos Theraputics will be there.
statements.context: Speaker announcement for RAMHT NYC 2024 (May 5th, 2024). The author adds that Lykos (formerly MAPS PBC) cannot say anything that would jeopardize its FDA review process, so the conversation will be 'appropriately boundried'.
statements.note: Own-event speaker plan; CONTROL candidate. Mentions Lykos's FDA review as ongoing, no call on its outcome.

statements.quote: Maybe you want to understand how AI will transform psychiatric care?
statements.context: Rhetorical question setting up the mdhub.ai and Videra Health panel at RAMHT NYC 2024; it presupposes that AI will transform psychiatric care.
statements.note: Embedded in a rhetorical question; a presupposition, not an explicit call. Borderline.

statements.quote: Dominik Middelmann mdhub.ai —helping physicians get their notes done—will be in the same room as Brett Talbot, Ph.D. from Videra Health —measuring outcomes with video capture AI models.
statements.context: Speaker lineup for RAMHT NYC 2024 (May 5th, 2024): AI-in-psychiatry panel.
statements.note: Own-event speaker plan; Videra is the author's organization; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: Between Osmind’s CMO and iRxReminder’s COO Fred Ma, M.D. on the same stage, we all might learn something.
statements.context: RAMHT NYC 2024 panel on how real-world evidence might affect future FDA approval of novel interventions.
statements.note: Own-event speaker plan; CONTROL candidate. The RWE-and-FDA framing is a question, not a call.

statements.quote: conference Co-Founder Grady Hannah of Nightware will be chatting with author Michelle Bernabe, R.N., about that very topic.
statements.context: RAMHT NYC 2024 session on how AI-guided digital therapeutics got to market.
statements.note: Own-event speaker plan; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: learn about sympathetic nervous system biology from James Lynch, M.D. , the founder of the Stellate Institute. It’s going to be a banger.
statements.context: Closing speaker mention for RAMHT NYC 2024 (stellate ganglion block for PTSD) and a forecast that the event will be a success.
statements.note: Own-event; 'banger' is hyperbole, the speaker plan is sincere. CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: This, to be clear, will keep happening. It’s in UnitedHealth Group’s (fiscal) interest.
statements.context: Second ransomware extortion of Change Healthcare (Optum, UnitedHealth Group) by RansomHub after the ALPHV/BlackCat attack. The author predicts continued attacks and argues UHG benefits financially from delayed claim payments.
statements.note: Author says he 'completely predicted' the second attack; restatement of an earlier call.

statements.quote: it would require fines from the DOJ at a scale I highly doubt they are willing to levy.
statements.context: Same post. The author says only very large DOJ fines would change UnitedHealth Group's behavior and doubts the DOJ will levy them.
statements.note: Negative call on the scale of DOJ enforcement.

statements.quote: That is our personal health information that is about to be sold to the dark web.
statements.context: RansomHub claims 4 TB of Change Healthcare data and threatens to sell it within 12 days. The author expects the protected health information to be sold on the dark web ('Regulators? Buckle up.').
statements.note: Adopts RansomHub's 12-day sale threat as an expectation.

statements.quote: More news as it breaks.
statements.context: Closing content promise about the Change Healthcare ransomware story.
statements.note: Own-newsletter content promise; low forecast value; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: reached out to RandomHub, which given the literal scammer profession of those involved may or may not turn out to have something to do with BlackCat/ALPHV
statements.context: Wired's Andy Greenberg contacted RansomHub (typo 'RandomHub' in the post). The author hedges on whether RansomHub is connected to BlackCat/ALPHV, the group behind the first Change Healthcare attack.
statements.note: Explicit hedge with no lean; borderline value.

statements.quote: Change, it turns out, will also deliver when the time is right. Not now.
statements.context: Change Healthcare's page promising nightly updates to the active payer list for Relay (a Change clearinghouse) is not updated and its link is dead text. Sarcastic closing line.
statements.note: Sarcasm; the sincere reading is that Change's payer-list updates are not happening now. Not a real expectation of delivery.

statements.quote: I am also hosting a real-life conference on the topic— RAMHT NYC 2024 —on May 5th.
statements.context: Intro to the Seroquel review; the author restates the RAMHT NYC 2024 conference on rapid-acting mental health treatments, May 5th, 2024.
statements.note: Own-event plan, restates earlier announcements; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: Seroquel is an effective treatment for bipolar depression and mania, but it might be the best drug for bipolar depression.
statements.context: First of six 'a priori' presumptions the author states before reviewing the evidence on Seroquel (quetiapine) in a coming series: 'Let's see how I do over the next series of reviews'.
statements.note: A priori bet about what the evidence review will show; resolvable by the author's later articles, not a future world state.

statements.quote: It helps people sleep, but it’s probably wildly inappropriate in terms of adverse effects to use it for this indication.
statements.context: Third 'a priori' presumption about Seroquel (quetiapine) used for sleep, stated before the evidence review series.
statements.note: A priori bet about the evidence; present-tense clinical judgment, logged for recall.

statements.quote: I suspect it’s broadly underdosed in clinical practice.
statements.context: Fourth 'a priori' presumption about Seroquel (quetiapine), stated before the evidence review series.
statements.note: A priori bet about current prescribing practice; resolvable by the author's later review.

statements.quote: I bet it doesn’t work at doses at which it’s commonly prescribed
statements.context: Fifth 'a priori' presumption about Seroquel (quetiapine), stated before the evidence review series.
statements.note: A priori bet about the evidence; explicit 'I bet' wording.

statements.quote: There have probably been a lot of lawsuits about it, for illegal marketing.
statements.context: Sixth 'a priori' presumption about Seroquel (quetiapine, AstraZeneca not named), stated before the evidence review series.
statements.note: A priori bet about past litigation; resolvable by the author's later review.

statements.quote: There’s more data on this medication and other indications, to stick around for the next episode.
statements.context: Closing content promise for the Seroquel series; earlier: 'some of the other concerns additional articles will address… foreshadowing!'
statements.note: Own-newsletter content promise; low forecast value; CONTROL candidate.
